case_name: Ram Ekbak Missir v Ram Niwash Pandey @ Sri Niwash Pandey and others
respondent: Ram Niwash Pandey @ Sri Niwash Pandey
facts: The FIR was registered under Section 302 IPC on a fardbayan of appellant on 5.8.1979.
After release, it was noticed that for unknown reasons they said proceedings were not listed before the C.J.M. from 1990 to the year 2000.
It is his further say that from the jail itself, he was trying to find out what had happened to the FIR lodged by him.
An FIR was registered under Section 302 IPC on a fardbayan of appellant on 5.8.1979.
The complainant has supported the complaint petition on S.A. and all the witnesses have supported/confirmed the occurrence.
It is the duty of the Courts to see that neither the victim nor the accused suffers by mischief of the Investigating Agency or the staff of the Court.
petitioner_arguments: The FIR was registered under Section 302 IPC on a fardbayan of appellant on 5.8.1979.
It is his further say that from the jail itself, he was trying to find out what had happened to the FIR lodged by him.
But this would hardly be a ground for dropping the prosecution where the accused are involved for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 147, 148 and 149 IPC.
court_reasoning: The complainant has supported the complaint petition on S.A. and all the witnesses have supported/confirmed the occurrence.
Therefore, cognizance is taken in the case.
It is the duty of the Courts to see that neither the victim nor the accused suffers by mischief of the Investigating Agency or the staff of the Court.
Further, at this stage, there was no necessity of making any observations on merits by the High Court as that is required to be decided at the time of trial or at the time of framing of charges.
holding: The appeal is allowed, the impugned judgment and order dated 11.10.2001 passed by the High Court of Patna in Cr.W.J.C. No.668 of 2000 is set aside.
The trial Court is directed to proceed further in the matter in accordance with law.
cases_cited: basis of the decision rendered by this Court in A.R. Antulay v. R.S
